text:
### Observed differences

- The relative use of A01 and A06 flipped: before, A01 ran in about 54 in 100 traces (107 of 200) and A06 in about 47 in 100 (93 of 200); in the later window A01 ran in about 47 in 100 and A06 in about 54 in 100 (93 vs 107). Their participation shares sum to all traces in each window, consistent with two alternatives at a shared decision point, and each 7-point move is larger than in about 79 in 100 of the random reference splits. [OCC001, OCC006]
- A12 took part in more traces in the later window: about 25 in 100 before (49 of 200) against about 32 in 100 after (63 of 200), a 7-point rise larger than in about 87 in 100 of the reference comparisons. [OCC012]
- Continuations after A12 were re-weighted: of A12's outgoing transitions, about 24 in 100 went to A03 before versus about 43 in 100 after, and A06 rose from about 2 to 17 in 100, while A01 fell from about 14 to 3, A09 from about 16 to 8 and A10 from about 20 to 11. This is the largest directional difference in the sample (exceeded by only about 2 in 100 reference splits) but rests on only about 49 versus 63 outgoing transitions. [DIR012]
- More traffic entered A12: A01's outgoing share to A12 rose from about 9 to 13 in 100, and A10's from about 3.5 to 11 in 100. [DIR001, DIR010]
- The outgoing mix of A01 and A06 also moved: after A01, the share continuing to A04 fell from about 13 to 4 in 100 while A02 rose from about 33 to 37 in 100; after A06, A02 fell from about 32 to 25 in 100 and A10 from about 23 to 18 in 100, while A03 and A09 each rose from about 7.5 to 13 in 100. [DIR001, DIR006]
- A04 appeared in fewer traces (about 27 in 100 before, about 22 in 100 after; 54 vs 45 traces), and its outgoing share to A03 dropped from about 41 to 24 in 100 while A06 rose from about 7 to 16 in 100; these proportions rest on fewer than 60 observations per window. [OCC004, DIR004]
- All other activities were essentially stable: A02, A03, A05, A07, A08, A09, A10, A13 and A14 stayed within about 2 participation points, and the dominant successor relations (A13→A14 at about 94 in 100, A14→A11 at about 91 rising to 98 in 100, A03→A13 at about 85 to 88 in 100) kept their roles with only marginal absolute shifts. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC005, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010, OCC011, OCC013, OCC014, DIR002, DIR003, DIR005, DIR007, DIR008, DIR013, DIR014]

### Inference

Support level: Weak hypothesis

The evidence suggests that in the later window existing alternative routes were taken with different frequencies: the choice between A01 and A06 moved from about 54/47 in favour of A01 to about 47/54 in favour of A06, and paths through A12 were used more often (about 25 in 100 traces before, about 32 in 100 after), with traces leaving A12 continuing more often to A03 or A06 and less often to A01, A09 or A10. [OCC001, OCC006, OCC012, DIR012, DIR001, DIR010]

The supporting signs are the exactly complementary A01/A06 counts in both windows (107/93 vs 93/107 of 200), the agreeing inflow indicators showing more transitions into A12 from A01 and A10, and the post-A12 redistribution being the largest directional difference in the sample; both activities involved are well observed in each window, so this is a shift between existing alternatives rather than a replacement of paths. [OCC001, OCC006, DIR001, DIR010, DIR012]

What is missing: the evidence provides no screening baseline, so the number of qualifying items cannot be compared with the number expected if nothing had changed; the participation moves reach empirical strengths of only about 0.79–0.87, meaning roughly one in five or more random re-splits would look at least as different; and the strongest item, the re-routing after A12, rests on about 49 versus 63 outgoing transitions. An important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is an ordinary sampling swing at a shared decision point, with the surrounding directional shifts merely mirroring the same traffic change rather than independently confirming it. [OCC001, OCC006, OCC012, DIR012]

Other differences: A04 was observed less often and its outgoing mix moved away from A03 (about 41 to 24 in 100) toward A06 and A10, on fewer than 60 observations per window; A14's outgoing became somewhat more concentrated on A11 (about 91 to 98 in 100) and A03's on A13 (about 85 to 88 in 100), both small absolute shifts. [OCC004, DIR004, DIR014, DIR003]
